title: Extension source descriptor — git-native import (D13/D22)

url.$comment: https-only git URL. The pattern is an ALLOWLIST (host + path classes): userinfo credentials ('@'), whitespace, backslashes and non-https transports are all structurally inexpressible rather than filtered — ssh:// and file:// are refused at this seam: the family distribution surface is https git URLs (D13).

slot.$comment: Secret-slot REFERENCE resolved by the host in its settings-map-declared secret store (private-repo credentials). There is no field anywhere in this schema that can hold a token VALUE — inline secrets are structurally invalid, not merely discouraged (D22).

pin.$comment: Recorded at install: the exact ref fetched + sha256 over the discovered content. Installs are digest-pinned; updates are ref-move + digest-change + manifest-diff (D15).

subpath.$comment: Directory inside the repo containing the extension manifest(s). No leading '/', no '..' segments (each segment starts alnum), no trailing slash.

value.$comment: The tag pattern / branch name / commit sha. Bounded, no whitespace/quotes — ref names are attacker-controlled input. Required for tag-pattern (glob, e.g. 'v*'), branch, commit-pin (40-hex or 64-hex, enforced by the branches below); release-tag resolves 'latest release' with no value.

ref.$comment: The exact git ref that was fetched (tag, branch-head sha or pinned commit).

digest.$comment: sha256 content digest over the discovered extension content — the consent surface names it; updates diff against it.

desiredStateDocument.title: GitOps desired-state document (admin-owned, D13/D22)

id.$comment: The named extension whose pin the list moves — reconcile touches ONLY entries listed here (D22).

enabled.$comment: Optional enable INTENT for the named extension — reconcile still never auto-enables imported code without consent (D13: consent is the gate, the list is only a pin-mover; hosts may ignore this field entirely).

extensions.$comment: There is deliberately NO remove/delete/uninstall field anywhere in this document: reconcile installs and moves pins only — never auto-enables, never deletes data; removal from the list parks the extension disabled and tombstone-able (D22). Deletion is structurally inexpressible.

desiredStateDocument.$comment: Admin-authored data ONLY — the model never authors desired state (ADR-0011 §7 / ADR-0030 §6, charter modelAuthorship).

localSourceDescriptor.title: Local git source — dev/test file-path variant (structurally distinct from the https root)

path.$comment: ABSOLUTE filesystem path to a local git repo (the sibling template repo, a dogfood checkout, a test fixture). Absolute-only and '..'-segment-free structurally — relative paths and traversal are rejected at this seam, never filtered. Host-side confinement (allowlisted parent roots, fail-closed off in production boots) is ADDITIONAL host policy on top (plan 32 Phase 3 local-source ruling).

localSourceDescriptor.$comment: The dev/test variant of the root descriptor: `local.path` replaces `url` — the two are structurally distinct shapes, and a local document NEVER validates against the root (which requires https `url` and has no `local` property). No `credentials` here: local file-path sources carry no private-repo auth (anything needing a credential is an https source). This definition exists so hosts validate local sources against the SAME schema artifact instead of hand-writing a per-host variant (D11) — production enforcement stays structural: the root descriptor is the production surface and remains https-only. Hosts MUST gate the local kind off in production boots (fail-closed) and confine paths to allowlisted roots.

$comment: Source descriptor (root) + GitOps desired-state document ($defs.desiredStateDocument) + dev/test local variant ($defs.localSourceDescriptor — NOT reachable from this root; production descriptors are https-only). Import pipeline (D13): resolve -> shallow fetch -> discover manifests -> schema-validate -> host-profile compatibility -> per-extension consent (capabilities, tier, provenance, digest in user language) -> pinned install (T0 data to the host store; T2 code to a sandbox dir never importable into process; T3 launch spec registered). A failed fetch leaves pins untouched and marks the source failing; manually-installed extensions are never re-pinned or removed.
